questions.stem: What is the function of the cell membrane?

options.text: To control what enters and leaves the cell

questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and controls which substances enter and leave the cell.

questions.stem: Where does aerobic respiration take place in the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, where glucose is broken down to release energy in the form of ATP.

questions.stem: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are small structures that read messenger RNA to build proteins. They are found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

options.text: Cell sap made of water and sugars

questions.explanation: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell and contains DNA organised into chromosomes, which controls cell activities by regulating gene expression.

questions.stem: Which structure produces lipids and steroid hormones?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes attached and is involved in producing lipids, steroid hormones, and detoxification.

questions.stem: What is the role of the Golgi apparatus?

options.text: To control what enters the cell
To modify, package, and distribute proteins

questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus consists of stacks of flattened membrane sacs that modify, package, and distribute proteins produced by the rough ER.

questions.stem: According to cell theory, where do all cells come from?

options.text: They form spontaneously from non-living matter
They are created by the nucleus

questions.explanation: Cell theory states that all cells arise from pre-existing cells. This is one of the three key principles alongside all organisms being composed of cells and cells being the basic unit of life.
